exercises.name: Brisk walk
cues: Walk fast enough that talking is possible but singing is not
Swing arms naturally
Aim for 7,000–10,000 steps a day
exercises.ibsNote: A 10–15 min walk after meals helps gas move through and eases bloating.

exercises.name: Post-meal digestion walk
cues: Start within 15 minutes of finishing a meal
Easy pace — this is for digestion and blood sugar, not burning calories
exercises.ibsNote: Gentle walking stimulates gut motility (helpful in IBS-C) and blunts post-meal glucose spikes.

exercises.name: Stair climbing
cues: Use the full foot on each step
Hold the rail lightly for balance
Walk down slowly to recover

exercises.name: Skipping rope
cues: Stay on the balls of your feet
Turn the rope from the wrists, not the shoulders
exercises.ibsNote: High-impact — skip on flare days, especially IBS-D.

exercises.name: Cycling (outdoor or stationary)
cues: Keep a steady cadence
Adjust the seat so the knee is slightly bent at the bottom

exercises.name: Bodyweight HIIT circuit
cues: Jumping jacks, squat jumps, mountain climbers, high knees
40 s work / 20 s rest, 3 rounds
exercises.ibsNote: Avoid within 2 hours of a big meal; intense jumping can trigger urgency.

exercises.name: Surya namaskar (sun salutation)
cues: Move with the breath — inhale up, exhale down
Keep the core gently engaged
Bend knees in forward folds if hamstrings are tight

exercises.name: Bodyweight squat
cues: Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out
Sit back as if onto a chair
Knees track over toes, chest up

exercises.name: Goblet squat
cues: Hold a dumbbell at the chest
Elbows inside knees at the bottom
Drive up through the heels

exercises.name: Reverse lunge
cues: Step back, lower until both knees are ~90°
Front knee stays over the ankle

exercises.name: Glute bridge
cues: Feet flat, hip-width
Squeeze glutes to lift hips; pause 2 s at the top

exercises.name: Push-up (knee or full)
cues: Hands under shoulders
Body in one straight line
Start on knees or against a wall if needed

exercises.name: Incline push-up (wall / table)
cues: Hands on a sturdy table edge
Lower chest to the edge, push back

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell row
cues: Support one hand and knee on a bench/chair
Pull the elbow towards the hip
Avoid twisting the torso

exercises.name: Resistance-band row
cues: Anchor the band at chest height
Squeeze shoulder blades together

exercises.name: Dumbbell shoulder press
cues: Brace the core, don't arch the lower back
Press straight up, lower to ear level

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
cues: Soft knees, hinge at the hips
Keep weights close to the legs
Flat back throughout

exercises.name: Chair triceps dip
cues: Hands on a stable chair edge
Lower until elbows are ~90°
Keep shoulders away from ears

exercises.name: Forearm plank
cues: Elbows under shoulders
Squeeze glutes, don't let hips sag
Breathe steadily
exercises.ibsNote: If planks increase bloating or pain, switch to dead bugs.

exercises.name: Dead bug
cues: Lower back pressed into the floor
Extend opposite arm and leg slowly
exercises.ibsNote: Gentle core work without high intra-abdominal pressure — good for sensitive guts.

exercises.name: Side plank
cues: Elbow under shoulder
Hips lifted in a straight line
Drop the bottom knee to make it easier

exercises.name: Mountain climbers
cues: Hands under shoulders
Drive knees towards the chest alternately

exercises.name: Cat–cow
cues: On hands and knees
Inhale: drop belly, lift chest; exhale: round the spine
Move slowly with breath
exercises.ibsNote: Massages the abdomen and can relieve trapped gas.

exercises.name: Pawanmuktasana (wind-relieving pose)
cues: Lie on your back, hug one knee then both to the chest
Hold 30 s, rock gently side to side
Breathe into the belly
exercises.ibsNote: Classic yoga pose for releasing gas and easing bloating.

exercises.name: Supine spinal twist
cues: Knees to one side, arms out wide
Look the other way; hold 30–60 s each side
exercises.ibsNote: Twists gently compress and release the colon — helpful for IBS-C.

exercises.name: Balasana (child's pose)
cues: Knees wide, big toes together, fold forward
Rest forehead down, breathe slowly
exercises.ibsNote: Calming; pairs well with belly breathing on flare days.

exercises.name: Malasana (garland squat)
cues: Feet wider than hips, sink into a deep squat
Palms together, elbows press knees open
exercises.ibsNote: Mimics the natural toileting posture; can help with constipation.

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic (belly) breathing
cues: One hand on chest, one on belly
Inhale 4 s through the nose so only the belly rises
Exhale 6 s slowly
exercises.ibsNote: Activates the 'rest and digest' response; evidence supports breathing work for IBS pain and stress.

exercises.name: Clockwise abdominal massage (I-L-U)
cues: Lying down, use flat fingers with gentle pressure
Trace I down the left side, L across and down, U from right up and across
Follow the direction of the colon, clockwise
exercises.ibsNote: Follows the colon's path and may relieve gas and constipation.

exercises.name: Anulom vilom (alternate-nostril breathing)
cues: Close the right nostril, inhale left; switch, exhale right
Keep it slow and unforced
exercises.ibsNote: Lowers stress, a strong IBS trigger.

exercises.name: Swimming
cues: Steady laps at a conversational pace
Mix strokes to work different muscles

exercises.name: Badminton / sport
cues: Warm up 5 min
A fun way to add NEAT and stay consistent
